		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Segment Information </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We have two reportable segments based on the engineering and production processes, and the products and services provided by each segment as follows: </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt 33.85pt;text-indent: -24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">1)</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 18pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">New units</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> are predominately highly engineered solutions to new requests from clients. New units also include standardized equipment such as engines and single stage steam turbines. The segment includes engineering, manufacturing, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">project management, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">packaging, testing, sales and administrative support. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt 33.85pt;text-indent: -24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2)</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 18pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Aftermarket parts and services</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> consist of support solutions for the existing population of installed equipment and the operation and maintenance of several types of energy plants. The segment includes engineering, manufacturing,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> project management,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> installation, commissioning, start-up and other field services, repairs, overhauls, refurbishment, sales and administrative support. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:9pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">These functions have been defined as the operating segments of the Company because they are the segments (1) that engage in business activities from which revenues are earned and expenses are incurred; (2) whose operating results are regul</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">arly reviewed by the Company</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x2019;s chief operating decision maker to make decisions about resources to be allocated to the segment and assess its performance; and (3) for which discrete financial information is available.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Unallocated amounts represent expenses and assets that cannot be assigned directly to either reportable segment because of their nature. Unallocated net expenses include certain corporate expenses, and research and development expenses. Assets that are directly assigned to the two reportable segments are trade accounts receivable, net inventories and goodwill. Unallocated assets include cash, prepaid expenses and other, deferred taxes, property, plant and equipment and intangible assets. There are no significant intercompany transactions between our reportable segments. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 1pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:1pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Effects of Currency Fluctuations </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Our results of operations are subject to both currency transaction risk and currency translation risk. We incur currency transaction risk whenever we or our</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> subsidiaries enter into a purchase or</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> sales transaction using a currency other than the functional currency </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">(usually local) </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">of the transacting entity. With respect to currency translation risk, our financial condition and results of operations are measured and recorded in the relevant functional currency and then translated into U.S.&nbsp;dollars for inclusion in our consolidated financial statements. Exchange rates between these currencies </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">and U.S.&nbsp;dollars historically</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> have fluctuated significantly and may continue to do so in the future. The most significant component of our revenues and costs is denominated in U.S.&nbsp;dollars. Euro-related revenues and costs are also significant. Historically, we have engaged in hedging strategies from time to time to reduce the effect of currency fluctuations on specific transactions. However, we have not sought to hedge currency translation risk. We expect to continue to engage in foreign currency hedging strategies going forward, but have not attempted to qualify our foreign currency hedges for hedge accounting treatment. Significant declines in the value of the euro relative to the U.S.&nbsp;dollar could have a material adverse effect on our consolidated financial condition and results of operations. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Revenues </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Our revenues are primarily generated through the sale of new units and aftermarket parts and services. Revenues are recognized as described in Note&nbsp;2, Summary of Significant Accounting Policies, in our notes to consolidated financial statements included herein in Item&nbsp;15, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Exhibits, Financial Statements and Schedules</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Cost of Sales </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Cost of sales includes raw materials, manufacturing and services related employee and overhead costs, freight and warehousing and product engineering. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Selling and Administrative Expenses </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Selling expenses consist of costs associated with marketing and sales. Administrative expenses are primarily management, corporate expenses and legal costs. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Research and Development Expenses </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Research and development expenses include payroll, employee benefits, and other labor related costs, depreciation, workstations and software costs associated with product development. These costs are expensed as incurred. Expenses for major projects are carefully evaluated to manage return on investment requirements. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">32</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt -27pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt -27pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Other Expense, Net </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Other expense, net includes those items that are non-operating in nature. Examples of items reported as other expense, net are equity in earnings of certain 50% or less owned affiliates, fair value adjustments of tradable emission allowances, fair value adjustments of contingent consideration, indemnification recoveries and the impact of currency exchange fluctuations. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Depreciation and Amortization </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Property, plant and equipment are reported at cost less accumulated depreciation, which is generally provided using the straight-line method over the respective estimated useful lives of the assets. Expenditures for improvements that extend the life of the asset are generally capitalized. Intangible assets primarily consist of amounts allocated to customer relationships, software and technology, trade names and other intangibles. All of the intangible assets are generally amortized using the straight-line method over their respective estimated useful lives. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Bookings and Backlog </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Effective July&nbsp;1, 2012, the Company elected to voluntarily change its policy for recording contract cancellations. Historically, contract cancellations were recorded as reductions in current period bookings. Beginning July&nbsp;1, 2012, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">contract cancellations are</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> recorded as direct adjustments to backlog with no impact on current period bookings. Contract cancellations in historical periods have not been material to bookings or backlog. The change in policy provides more relevant information about current market activity by recognizing economic events in the periods in which they occur. In accordance with this policy, material contract cancellations di</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">rectly adjusting backlog are</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> separately disclosed. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">New Units </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Bookings represent firm orders placed for a specific scope of supply during the period, whether or not filled. The elapsed time from booking to completion of performance is typically four to fifteen months (and potentially longer for certain major projects). The backlog of unfilled orders includes amounts based on signed contracts as well as agreed letters of authorization that management has determined are likely to be performed. Although backlog represents business that is considered firm, cancellations or scope adjustments may occur. In certain cases, cancellation of a contract provides us with the opportunity to bill for certain incurred costs and penalties. Backlog is adjusted to reflect currency exchange rates as of the date the backlog is reported. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Aftermarket Parts and Services </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Bookings represent firm orders placed for a specific scope of supply during the period, whether or not filled. Backlog primarily consists of unfilled parts orders and open repair and field service orders. The elapsed time from order entry to completion can be one day to 12&nbsp;months depending on the complexity of the order. Backlog is adjusted to reflect currency exchange rates as of the date the backlog is reported. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:13.5pt 0pt 0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Letters of Credit, Bank Guarantees and Surety Bonds </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">In the ordinary course of our business, we make use of letters of credit, bank guarantees and surety bonds. We use both performance bonds, ensuring the performance of our obligations under various contracts to which we are a party, and advance payment bonds, which ensure that clients that place purchase orders with us and make advance payments under such contracts are reimbursed to the extent we fail to deliver under the contract. Under the revolvi</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">ng portion of our Amended</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;"> Credit Facility, we are entitled to have up to </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">$1,1</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">00.0 of letters of credit outstanding at any time, subject to certain conditions. From time to time, we also use letters of credit and bank guarantees issued by banks offering uncommitted lines of credit, which are n</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">ot limited by the Amended</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;"> Credit Facili</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">ty.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt -25.2pt 0pt 0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt -25.2pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			&nbsp;

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Revenues.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp; Revenues were </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">$3,032.6</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> for the year</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> ended </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">, compared to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">$2,736.4</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> for the year </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">ended </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">, an increase of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">$296.2</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> or </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">10.8%</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">. Generally, oil prices and other macroeconomic conditions that affect the oil and gas industry have an impact on our business over an extended period of time. On a quarterly or annual basis, however, there is typically not a direct correlation of short-term volatility in these factors to our periodic financial results. Fluctuations in revenues and bookings are generally due to variability in the timing and size of very large orders in the new units segment, which is typical in the oil and gas industry. This occurs because our equipment, in many cases, is used in very large capital projects that take years to plan and execute, and such projects do not occur on a regular or consistent basis due to their size, location</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">, technical resources, client capital expenditure constraints</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> and long-term relationship to global energy supply and demand. While a change in these factors at a macroeconomic level will tend to have a corresponding overall effect on our revenue, the timing of such effect on our quarterly or even annual revenues is not directly correlated because of the very long lead times required to evaluate the macroeconomic landscape and then plan</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">, permit</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> and execute the projects. Furthermore, the highly engineered nature of our worldwide products and services does not easily lend itself to measuring the impact of price, volume and mix on changes in our to</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">tal revenues from year to year. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Nevertheless, based on factors such as measures of labor hours and purchases from suppliers, revenues increased due to highe</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">r volume during the year</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> ended </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">as a result of</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> the </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">timing issues discussed above</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;Price i</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">ncreases in the aftermarket parts and services segment also contributed incremental revenues, albeit to a much lesser extent.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">These increases were partially off</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">set by negative impacts from our</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> six pig manure treatment facilities in Spain which we acquired in our acquisition of Guascor.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Spanish government published a draft regulation at the end of January 2014 that reflects a reduction in the tariffs of approximately 37%, which, if enacted, would be retroactive to July 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;In connection with the draft regulation being issued, 2013 revenues </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">are lower by approximately $23.7</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> as a result of the retroactive reduction of the tariffs which partially offsets the overall increase in revenues.&nbsp;&nbsp;An adverse translation impact of foreign currency f</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">luctuations of approximately $28.5</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">, resulting from a stronger U.S. dollar, also partially offset the increase in reven</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">ues.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp; 		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Bookings and backlog.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Bookings for the year</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> ended </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, were </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$2,941.4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> compared to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$3,162.8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> for the year</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> ended </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, a de</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">crease of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$221.4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> or </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">7.0%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">. The Company believes that the de</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">cre</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ase in bookings is due to</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">(1) dela</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ys in major upstream projects by our end-user clients in an effort to address their escalating capital costs relating to those projects and (2) engineering resource constraints being experienced by our end-user clients and their third-party contractors.&nbsp;&nbsp;In </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">addition, in view of the proposed</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> change in the tariffs </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">reflected </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">in the draft Spanish regulation discussed above, our 2013 aftermarket bookings </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">are lower by approximately $23.7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> related to the retroactive reduction of the tariffs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Backlog was </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$2,849.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> at December 31, 2013, compared to $2,946.0 at December 31, 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font>
		</p>

The </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Company believes that the decrease</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> in bookings is </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">due to</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">(1) delays in major upstream projects by our end-user clients in an effort to address their escalating capital costs relating to those projects and (2) engineering resource constraints being experienced by our end-user clients and their third-party contractors.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Backlog was </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$2,187.7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> at </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, compare</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">d to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$2,370.6</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> at </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Aftermarket Parts and Services</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Revenues.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenues for this segment were </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$1,508.5</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;for the year</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> ended </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2013</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, compared to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$1,434.8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;for the year</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> ended </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">December 31, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, an increase of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$73.7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> or </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">5.1%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Generally, oil prices and other macroeconomic conditions that affect the oil and gas industry have an impact on our business over an extended period of time, but less so in this segm</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ent. On a quarterly or annual basis, however, there is typically not a meaningful correlation of those factors to our periodic financial results. During the year ended December 31, 2013, the Company experienced aftermarket growth in most geographic segments, but particularly in Europe and Latin America, resulting in higher volumes.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In view of the proposed</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> change in the tariffs </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">reflected </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">in the draft Spanish regulation discussed above, our 2013 revenues </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">are lower by approximately $23.7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> related to the retroactive reduction of the tariffs</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> which partially offsets the overall increase in revenues.&nbsp;&nbsp;An adverse translation impact of foreign currency f</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">luctuations of approximately $19</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.3, resulting from a stronger U.S. dollar, partially offset the increase in revenues.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Gross profit.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;Gross profit was </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$535.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;for the year ended December 31, 2013, compared to $516.2&nbsp;for the year ended December 31, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;Gross profit as a percentage of segment revenues for the year ended December 31, 2013, of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">35.5%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> decreased from 36.0% for the year ended December 31, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Gross profit as a percentage of revenues </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">declined </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">by approximately 0.9% </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">because of the</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> proposed</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> change in the tariffs </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">reflected </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">in the draft Spanish regulation discussed above which was substantially offset by</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> mix, operating leverage and price increases.</font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Fixed asset impairment of cogeneration facilities.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In view of the proposed</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> change in the tariffs </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">reflected </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">in the draft Spanish regulation discussed above, we have decided to suspend the operations at our six pig manure </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">treatment </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">facilities, although discussions with the Spanish government are ongoing.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">On January&nbsp;2, 2013, the American Taxpayer Relief Act (&#x201C;ATRA&#x201D;) of 2012 was signed into law.&nbsp;Some of the provisions were retroactive to January&nbsp;1, 2012, including the exclusion from U.S. federal taxable income of certain interest, dividends, rents, and royalty income of foreign affiliates, as well as the tax benefits of the credits associated with that income and an extension of the research and experimentation credit.&nbsp;As required by U.S. GAAP, the tax rate above reflects the tax law that was in place as of December&nbsp;31, 2012. Had the ATRA been enacted prior to January&nbsp;1, 2013, our overall tax expense would have been approximately $4.4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> lower at an overall effe</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ctive rate of approximately 32.1%.&nbsp;This $4.4 benefit was</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> reflected in the first quart</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">er of 2013 as a discrete event.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Noncontrolling interest.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> Noncontrolling interest includes the share of net income and net losses in consolidated entities that are not 100% owned by us. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Bookings and backlog.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;Bookings for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, were $3,162.8 compared to $2,858.6 for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, an increase of $304.2 or 10.6%. The markets for our products and services remained strong in 2012, and we achieved record levels of bookings in both segments. The increase in new unit bookings reflected continuing recovery across worldwide energy infrastructure markets, with major orders from the midstream and upstream markets. The increase in aftermarket parts and services bookings reflected the ongoing economic improvement in most regions, particularly the Middle East and Latin America. Guascor contributed approximately $109.5 million of incremental bookings in 2012 resulting from the effect of having a full year of Guascor bookings in 2012 versus only eight months in the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011. The increase was partially offset by a decrease in market activity in the power sector. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

In the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, approximately $410.0 and $60.0 were reflected in the Company&#x2019;s new units and aftermarket bookings, respectively</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font>

During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, backlog was directly reduced by $58.4 as a result of a contract cancellation.</font>

The Company experienced lower volumes in the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, because of the timing of bookings in 2010 and the cycle times necessary to convert those orders to shipments as well as a flood in our Wellsville facility. Guascor contributed approximately $24.4 million of incremental revenues in 2012 resulting from the effect of having a full year of Guascor revenues in 2012 versus only eight months in the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011. Gross profit, as a percentage of segment revenues, was 16.6% for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, compared to 19.4% for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011. We experienced decreased gross profit as a percentage of sales in our new units segment because the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, included certain higher margin projects, leading to a less favorable mix for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012. The increase in new units as a percentage of total revenues also resulted in a higher allocation of fixed costs. The net effect of these items was partially offset by the flood in May 2011, which had an unfavorable impact on the absorption of fixed costs for our Wellsville facility, resulting in higher cost of sales and reduced gross profit for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011.</font>

As a percentage of segment revenues, income from operations was 9.1% for 2012 compared to 10.2% for 2011. Income from operations as a percentage of revenues decreased compared to the prior year as a result of the factors discussed above, partially offset by higher operating leverage on selling, general and administrative expenses. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Bookings and backlog.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;New units bookings for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, were $1,630.0 compared to $1,500.3&nbsp;for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011. The increase in new unit bookings reflected continuing recovery across worldwide energy infrastructure markets, with major orders from the midstream and upstream markets. During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, the Company was awarded contracts for compression equipment and services, which include up to 80 DATUM</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:7.5pt;font-size:4pt;top:-4pt;position:relative;line-height:100%">&#xAE;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> compressor trains that will be installed on eight FPSO vessels. In the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, approximately $410.0 was reflected in the Company&#x2019;s new units bookings. Guascor contributed approximately $16.9 million of incremental bookings in 2012 resulting from the effect of having a full year of Guascor bookings in 2012 versus only eight months in the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011. The increase in bookings was partially offset by a decrease in market activity in the power sector. Backlog was $2,370.6&nbsp;at December&nbsp;31, 2012, compared to $2,075.2&nbsp;at December&nbsp;31, 2011. We had record year-end backlog at December&nbsp;31, 2012, resulting from the continuing growth in our served industry markets, especially the upstream and midstream oil and gas markets. During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, backlog was directly reduced by $58.4 as a result of a contract cancellation.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Aftermarket Parts and Services </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Revenues.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;Revenues for this segment were $1,434.8&nbsp;for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, compared to $1,229.4&nbsp;for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, an increase of $205.4 or 16.7%. Generally, oil prices and other macroeconomic conditions that affect the oil and gas industry have an impact on our business over an extended period of time, but less so in this segment. On a quarterly or annual basis, however, there is typically not a meaningful correlation of those factors to our periodic financial results. During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, the Company experienced aftermarket growth in most geographic segments, but particularly in the Middle East and Latin America. The effect of having a full year of Guascor revenues in 2012 versus only eight months in the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, was approximately $94.2. An adverse translation impact of foreign currency fluctuations decreased aftermarket revenues by approximately $64.3 year over year.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Gross profit.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;Gross profit was $516.2 for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, compared to $433.6 for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011. Gross profit, as a percentage of segment revenues, was 36.0% for 2012 compared to 35.3% for 2011. Gross profit as a percentage of revenues increased principally due to a lower allocation of fixed costs resulting from a decrease in aftermarket revenues as a percentage of total revenues.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Income from operations.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;Income from operations was $323.2 for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, compared to $252.7 for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011. As a percentage of segment revenues, income from operations was 22.5% for 2012 compared to 20.6% for 2011. The changes in income from operations and income from operations as a percentage of segment revenues resulted principally from the reasons discussed above as well as higher operating leverage on selling, general and administrative expenses.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Bookings and backlog.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;Bookings for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, were $1,532.8,&nbsp;compared to $1,358.3&nbsp;for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011. The increase in aftermarket parts and services bookings reflected the ongoing economic improvement in most regions, particularly the Middle East and Latin America. The effect of having a full year of Guascor bookings in 2012 versus only eight months in the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, was approximately $92.6. During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, the Company was awarded contracts for compression equipment and services, which include up to 80 DATUM</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:7.5pt;font-size:4pt;top:-4pt;position:relative;line-height:100%">&#xAE;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> compressor trains that will be installed on eight FPSO vessels. In the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, approximately $60.0 was reflected in the Company&#x2019;s aftermarket bookings. Backlog was $575.4&nbsp;at December&nbsp;31, 2012, compared to $477.4&nbsp;at December&nbsp;31, 2011.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">On December&nbsp;28, 2007, the Company executed a &#x20AC;23.0 transaction (approximately $31.6), including a committed line of credit, that was used to fund construction of a test bench facility (the &#x201C;Facility&#x201D;) at the Port of LeHavre, France, for full load, full power testing of compressors powered by gas turbines and electric motors. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company is leasing the Facility and 14&nbsp;acres of land underlying the Facility under a lease (the &#x201C;Lease&#x201D;) pursuant to which the Company agreed to bear certain rights, obligations and expenses related to the Facility and land. The Port of Le Havre owns the land and allows access to the Facility and occupancy under the terms of a 30-year ground lease.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company is required to pay rent to the lessor during the initial base term of the Lease from the date construction was completed in an amount equal to the total of interest payable by the lessor on the outstanding principal amount of the debt incurred to construct the facility. Interest is generally determined by reference to the EURIBOR rate, plus an applicable margin of between 125 and 250&nbsp;basis points. The Company has entered into an interest rate swap agreement to minimize the economic impact of unexpected fluctuations in interest rates on the Lease, which is more fully described in Note 15 to the consolidated financial statements included herein in Item&nbsp;15, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Exhibits, Financial Statements and Schedules</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">. &nbsp;</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:normal;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:left;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Critical Accounting Policies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Note&nbsp;2, Summary of Significant Accounting Policies, in the notes to consolidated financial statements included in this </font><br /><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Form&nbsp;10-K in Item&nbsp;15, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Exhibits, Financial Statements and Schedules</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, includes a summary of significant accounting policies and methods used in the preparation of the consolidated financial statements. The following summarizes what we believe are the critical accounting policies and methods we use:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Revenue recognition &#x2014; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We recognize revenue when it is realized or realizable and earned. Generally, we consider revenue realized or realizable and earned when we have persuasive evidence of an arrangement, delivery of the product or service has occurred, the sales price is fixed or determinable and collectability is reasonably assured. Delivery does not occur until products have been shipped or services have been provided to the client, risk of loss has transferred to the client, and either any required client acceptance has been obtained (or such provisions have lapsed) or we have objective evidence that the criteria specified in the client acceptance provisions have been satisfied. The amount of revenue related to any contingency is not recognized unt</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">il the contingency is resolved.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt;text-indent:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Multiple-element arrangements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">A substantial portion of our arrangements are multiple-element revenue arrangements or contracts, which may include any combination of designing, developing, manufacturing, modifying and commissioning complex products to customer specifications and providing services related to the performance of such products. These contracts normally take up to fifteen months to complete. Provided that the separate deliverables have value to the client on a stand-alone basis, we use the selling price hierarchy described below to determine how to separate multiple element revenue arrangements into separate units of accounting and how to allocate the arrangement consideration among those separate units of accounting: </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<p style="border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;">Vendor-specific objective evidence.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;">Third-party evidence if vendor-specific objective evidence is not available.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;">Estimated selling price determined in the same manner as that used to determine the price at which we sell the deliverables on a stand-alone basis if neither vendor-specific objective evidence nor third-party evidence is available.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Our sales arrangements do not include a general right of return of the delivered unit(s). If it is determined that the separate deliverables do not have value on a stand-alone basis, the arrangement is accounted for as one unit of accounting, which results in revenue being recognized when the last</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> undelivered unit is delivered.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 9pt;text-indent:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Percentage of completion</font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;"> contracts</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We enter</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> into </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">certain</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> contracts with expanded construction-type scope and risk.&nbsp;&nbsp;These contractual arrangements have a scope of activity that differs in substance from the scope of deliverables found in our traditional sales arrangements. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Revenue from these contracts is recognized as contract performance progresses using the </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">percentage of completion</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"> method. We estimate the progress towards completion to determine the amount of revenue and profit to be recognized in each reporting period, based upon estimates of the total labor cost and labor converted material cost to complete the project; estimates of the project schedule and completion date; estimates of the extent of progress toward completion; and amounts of any probable claims and change orders included in revenue. Progress is generally based upon a labor dollars approach but we also use alternative methods including cost to cost, depending on the type of arrangement. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">At the outset of each contract, we prepare a detailed analysis of our estimated cost to complete the project. Risks relating to service delivery, usage, productivity and other factors are considered in the estimation process. Our project personnel periodically evaluate the estimated costs, claims, change orders and percentage of completion at the project level. The recording of profits and losses on contracts requires an estimate of the total profit or loss over the life of each contract. This estimate requires consideration of total contract value, change orders and claims, less costs incurred and estimated costs to complete. Our contracts often contain provisions for liquidated damages should we not meet certain performance requirements, including completion of the project in accordance with a scheduled timeline. We generally include an </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">45</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt -27pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">estimate of liqu</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">idated damages as a reduction of revenue</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"> when it is deemed probable that they will be paid. Profits are recorded based upon the product of estimated contract profit at completion times the current </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">percentage of completion</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"> for the contract.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">At least quarterly, significant projects are reviewed in detail by senior management. There are many factors that impact future costs, including but not limited to weather, inflation, labor and community disruptions, timely availability of materials, productivity and </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">other factors as outlined in Item 1A,</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Risk Factors</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">, in this Form 10-K</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"> These factors can affect the accuracy of our estimates and materially impact our future reported earnings.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We estimate the future costs that will be incurred related to sales arrangements to determine whether any arrangement will result in a loss. These costs include material, labor and overhead. Factors influencing these future costs include the availability of materials and skilled laborers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We record provisions for estimated losses on uncompleted contracts in the period in which such losses are identified.&nbsp;&nbsp;The cumulative effects of revisions to contract revenue and estimated completion costs are recorded in the accounting period in which the amounts become evident and can be reasonably estimated.&nbsp;&nbsp;These revisions can include such items as the effects of change orders and claims, warranty claims, liquidated damages or other contractual penalties, adjustments for audit findings on U.S. government contracts and contract closeout settlements.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;Durin</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">g 2013 and 2012, we did not record any provisions for estimated losses on uncompleted contracts.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Inventories</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;&#x2014; We purchase materials for the manufacture of components for use in both our new units and aftermarket parts and services segments. The decision to purchase a set quantity of a particular item is influenced by several factors including: current and projected cost; future estimated availability; existing and projected contracts to produce certain items; and the estimated needs for our aftermarket parts and services business. We value our inventory at the lower of cost (generally, first-in first-out or average) or market value. We estimate the net realizable value of our inventories and establish reserves to reduce the carrying amount of these inventories to the lower of cost or market (net realizable value) as necessary. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Income taxes&nbsp;&#x2014; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Our effective tax rate is based on income before income taxes and the tax rates applicable to that income in the various jurisdictions in which we operate. An estimated effective tax rate for the year is applied to the Company&#x2019;s quarterly operating results. In the event that there is a significant unusual or discrete item recognized, or expected to be recognized, in the Company&#x2019;s quarterly operating results, the tax attributable to that item is separately calculated and recorded at the same time as the unusual or discrete item. We consider the resolution of prior tax matters to be such items. Significant judgment is required in determining our effective tax rate and in evaluating tax positions. We establish tax accruals for uncertain tax positions if it is more-likely-than-not that the position will not be sustained upon examination through any appeals and litigation processes based on the technical merits of the position&nbsp;at the largest amount of benefit that is greater than 50&nbsp;percent likely of being realized upon ultimate settlement. We adjust these accruals in light of changing facts and circumstances. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Tax regulations may require items of income and expense to be included in the tax return that are not reflected in the current year&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements. Some of these differences are permanent, such as expenses that are not deductible on the tax return, and some are temporary differences, such as depreciation expense, which is recognized over different periods in the income tax return and the consolidated financial statements. Temporary differences create deferred tax assets and liabilities. Deferred tax assets generally represent items that can be used as tax deductions or credits in the tax return in future years for which we have already recorded the tax benefit in the consolidated financial statements. We establish valuation allowances for our deferred tax assets when it is more-likely-than-not that the amount of expected future taxable income will not support the use of the deduction or credit. Deferred tax liabilities generally represent tax expense recognized in the consolidated financial statements for which the related tax payment has been deferred or an expense which we have already taken a deduction on the income tax return, but has not yet been recognized as expense in the consolidated financial statements. As a result, the effective tax rate reflected in the consolidated financial statements may be different than the tax rate reported in income tax returns.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 1pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:1pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Employee benefit plans</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;&#x2014; We provide a range of benefits to employees and retired former employees, including pensions, post-retirement, postemployment and healthcare benefits. Determining the cost associated with such benefits is dependent on various actuarial assumptions, including discount rates, expected return on plan assets, compensation increases, employee mortality and turnover rates, and healthcare cost trend rates. Independent actuaries perform the required calculations to determine expense in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Actual results may differ from the actuarial assumptions and are generally accumulated and amortized over future periods. We review our actuarial assumptions at each measurement date and make modifications to the assumptions based on then current rates and trends if appropriate to do so. The discount rate, the rate of compensation increase and the expected long-term rates of return on plan assets are </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">46</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt -27pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">determined as of the measurement date. The discount rate reflects a rate at which pension benefits could be effectively settled. The discount rate is established and based primarily on the yields of high quality fixed-income investments available and expected to be available during the period to maturity of the pension and post-retirement benefits. We also review the yields reported by Moody&#x2019;s on AA corporate bonds as of the measurement date. The rate of compensation increase is dependent on expected future compensation levels. The expected long-term rates of return are projected to be the rates of return to be earned over the period until the benefits are paid. Accordingly, the long-term rates of return should reflect the rates of return on present investments, expected contributions to be received during the current year and on reinvestments over the period. The rates of return utilized reflect the expected rates of return during the periods for which the payment of benefits is deferred. The expected long-term rate of return on plan assets used is based on what is realistically achievable based on the types of assets held by the plans and the plan&#x2019;s investment policy. We review each plan and its returns and asset allocations to determine the appropriate expected long-term rate of return on plan assets to be used. We believe that the assumptions utilized in recording our obligations under our plans are reasonable based on input from our actuaries, outside investment advisors and information as to assumptions used by plan sponsors. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">A 1% change in the medical cost trend rate assumed for post-retirement benefits would have the following effects for the year ended and as of December&nbsp;31, 2013: </font>
