			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Effective January 1, 2013, the Company adopted FASB ASU 2013-02, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Comprehensive Income (Topic 220): Reporting of Amounts Reclassified Out of Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> (&#x201C;ASU 2013-02&#x201D;). The amendments in ASU 2013-02 are intended to improve the transparency of reporting reclassifications out of accumulated other comprehensive income by requiring an entity to report the effect of significant reclassifications out of accumulated other comprehensive income on the respective line items in net income if the amount being reclassified is required under U.S. GAAP to be reclassified in its entirety to net income. For other amounts that are not required under U.S. GAAP to be reclassified in their </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Effective January 1, 2013, the Company adopted FASB ASU 2013-01, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Balance Sheet (Topic 210): Clarifying the Scope of Disclosures about Offsetting Assets and Liabilities</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> (&#x201C;ASU 2013-01&#x201D;). The amendments in ASU 2013-01 require an entity to disclose both gross information and net information about both instruments and transactions eligible for offset in the statement of financial position and instruments and transactions subject to an agreement similar to a master netting arrangement.&nbsp;&nbsp;The enhanced disclosures are intended to enable users of an entity&#x2019;s financial statements to understand and evaluate the effect of master netting arrangements on an entity&#x2019;s financial position, including the effect or potential effect of rights of setoff associated with certain financial instruments and derivative instruments.&nbsp;&nbsp;The adoption of ASU 2013-01 did not have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements. The required disclosures have been included in Note 15, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Financial Instruments</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of these financial statements.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In February 2013</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> the FASB issued ASU 2013-04, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Liabilities (Topic 405): Obligations Resulting from Joint and Several Liability Arrangements for Which the Total Amount of the Obligation is Fixed at the Reporting Date </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">(&#x201C;ASU 2013-04&#x201D;). The amendments in ASU 2013-04 provide guidance for the recognition, measurement and disclosure of obligations resulting from joint and several liability arrangements for which the total amount of the obligation is fixed at the reporting date, except for obligations addressed within existing guidance in U.S. GAAP. In accordance with the amendments, an entity will measure the obligation as the sum of (1) the amount the reporting entity agreed to pay on the basis of its arrangements among its co-obligors, and (2) any additional amount the reporting entity expects to pay on behalf of its co-obligors. The amendments in ASU 2013-04 also require an entity to disclose the nature and amount of the obligation</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> as well as other information about those obligations. The amendments in ASU 2013-04 are effective for fiscal years, and interim periods within those years, beginning after December 15, 2013. The amendments should be applied retrospectively to all prior periods presented for those obligations resulting from joint and several liability arrangements that exist at the beginning of the fiscal year of adoption. The adoption of ASU 2013-04 is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In March 2013</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> the FASB issued ASU 2013-05, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Foreign Currency Matters (Topic 830): Parent&#x2019;s Accounting for the Cumulative Translation Adjustment upon Derecognition of Certain Subsidiaries or Groups of Assets within a Foreign Entity or of an Investment in a Foreign Entity </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">(&#x201C;ASU 2013-05&#x201D;). The amendments in ASU 2013-05 resolve the diversity in practice in applying Subtopic 810-10, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Consolidation</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, and Subtopic 830-30, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Foreign Currency Matters</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, when a reporting entity ceases to have a controlling financial interest in a subsidiary within a foreign entity. The amendments in ASU 2013-05 require the reporting entity to release any related cumulative translation adjustment into net income only if the sale or transfer results in the complete or substantially complete liquidation of the foreign entity in which the subsidiary resided.&nbsp;&nbsp;For an equity method investment that is a foreign entity, a pro rata portion of the cumulative translation adjustment should be released into net income upon a partial sale of s</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">uch an equity method investment</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> if significant influence is retained.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, the amendments clarify that the sale of an investment in a foreign entity includes both (1) events that result in the loss of a controlling financial interest in a foreign entity; and (2) events that result in an acquirer obtaining control of an acquiree in which it held an equity interest immediately before the acquisition date (step acquisition). The amendments in ASU 2013-05 are effective prospectively for fiscal years, and interim periods within those years, beginning after December 15, 2013. The amendments should be applied prospectively to derecognition events occurring after the effective date. The adoption of ASU 2013-05 is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In April 2013</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> the FASB issued ASU 2013-07, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Presentation of Financial Statements (Topic 205): Liquidation Basis of Accounting </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">(&#x201C;ASU 2013-07&#x201D;). The amendments in ASU 2013-07 clarify when an entity should apply the liquidation basis of accounting and provide principles for the recognition and measurement of associated assets and liabilities. In accordance with the amendments, the liquidation basis is used when liquidation is imminent.&nbsp;&nbsp;Liquidation is considered imminent when the likelihood is remote that the organization will return from liquidation and either: (a) a plan for liquidation is approved by the person or persons with the authority to make such a plan effective and the likelihood is remote that the execution of the plan will be blocked by other parties; or (b) a plan for liquidation is being imposed by other forces.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amendments in ASU 2013-07 are effective prospectively for entities that determine liquidation is imminent for reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2013. The adoption of ASU 2013-07 is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;text-indent:10.1pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

The amendments in ASU 2013-10 permit the Fed Funds Effective Swap Rate to be used as a U.S. benchmark interest rate for hedge accounting purposes in addition to U.S. Treasury rates and the London Interbank Offered Rate. The update also removes the restriction on using different benchmark rates for similar hedges. The amendments in ASU 2013-10 are effective prospectively for qualifying new or redesignated hedging relationships entered into on or after July 17, 2013. The adoption of ASU 2013-10 is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In July 2013</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> the FASB issued ASU 2013-11, </font><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Income Taxes (Topic 740): Presentation of an Unrecognized Tax Benefit When a Net Operating Loss Carryforward, a Similar Tax Loss, or a Tax Credit Carryforward Exists </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">(&#x201C;ASU 2013-11&#x201D;). The amendments in ASU 2013-11 clarify that an unrecognize</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">d tax benefit, or a portion of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">an unrecognized tax benefit, should be presented in the financial statements as a reduction to a deferred tax asset for a net operating loss carryforward, a similar tax loss, or a tax credit carryforward if such settlement is required or expected in the event the uncertain tax position is disallowed.&nbsp;&nbsp;In situations where a net operating loss carryforward, a similar tax loss, or a tax credit carryforward is not available at the reporting date under the tax law of the applicable jurisdiction or the tax law of the jurisdiction does not require, and the entity does not intend to use the deferred tax asset for such purpose, the unrecognized tax benefit should be presented in the financial statements as a liability and should not be combined with deferred tax assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amendments in ASU 2013-11 are effective prospectively for fiscal years, and interim periods within those years, beginning after December 15, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Retrospective application is permitted.&nbsp;&nbsp;The adoption of ASU 2013-11 is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">On January 4, 2012, the Company acquired Synchrony, Inc. (&#x201C;Synchrony&#x201D;), a technology development company with a portfolio of technologies and products including active magnetic bearings, low power, high speed motors and generators, and power electronics for clean, efficient and reliable rotating machinery.&nbsp;&nbsp;Founded in 1993, Synchrony is headquartered in Roanoke County, Virginia, where it operates an ISO 9001 certified production facility, in-house test cells for high-speed machinery, a model shop for prototype fabrication and assembly and an on-site software integration laboratory.&nbsp;&nbsp;Pursuant to the terms of the acquisition agreement, the Company acquired Synchrony for approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">48.8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, net of cash acquired,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> at which time </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Synchrony</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> became a </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">100</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">%-owned indirect subsidiary of the Company</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The acquisition gives the Company the ability to integrate Synchrony&#x2019;s active magnetic bearing capability into its product development process and to offer oil-free solutions in high speed rotating equipment applications, the benefits of which include reduced footprint and weight of the application and more environmentally-friendly applications. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The agreement include</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">d</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> the potential for additional contingent consideration of up to a maximum of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$10.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">based on technical milestones and business performance</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, 2013, the Company had made </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">all contractually required</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> contingent consideration payments </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">totaling</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$4.7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> to the sellers of Synchrony.</font>

(&#x201C;Guascor&#x201D;) pursuant to a Share Purchase Agreement (the &#x201C;SPA&#x201D;), at which time Guascor became a </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">100%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">-owned subsidiary of the Company. Guascor is a supplier of diesel and gas engines and provides customized energy solutions across worldwide energy infrastructure markets based upon reciprocating engine power systems technologies. Pursuant to the SPA, the Company paid approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$283.5</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, net of cash acquired, assumed </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$253.4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of debt, and delivered </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">5,033,172</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> shares of Company common stock at closing. The total purchase price was approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$543.2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, subject to a further cash purchase price adjustment to the extent that net debt (debt minus cash), as defined in the SPA, is different from the net debt at the end of business on the date of closing, which is being contested by the parties and could take several months and potentially years to finalize and could be material.</font>

D-R Arabia executes manufacturing, repair, and other services, and provides technical expertise and training in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The Company and ARPIC each own approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">50%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of D-R Arabia. 			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In 2008, the Company entered into an agreement by which it acquired a noncontrolling interest in Ramgen Power Systems, LLC (&#x201C;Ramgen&#x201D;), a privately-held company that is developing compressor technology that applies proven supersonic aircraft technology to ground-based air and gas compressors.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to receiving a noncontrolling interest, the Company received an option to acquire the business of Ramgen at a price of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$25.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and a royalty commitment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The option is exercisable at any time through </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">November 10, 2014</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">. The Company has made investments totaling </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$34</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, which have resulted in an aggregate noncontrolling interest of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">42.2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> at December 31</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s maximum exposure to loss on its investment in Ramgen is limited to amounts invested plus any amounts the Company may choose to invest in the future. In determining whether the Company should consolidate Ramgen, the Company considered that its board participation, ownership interest and the option to acquire would not give the Company the power to direct the activities of Ramgen and, consequently, would not result in the Company being the primary beneficiary. The investment in Ramgen is being accounted for under the equity method of accounting, and the amount of the investment recorded in other noncurrent assets on the consolidated balance sheet is </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$29</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> at December 31</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, 2013.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 2.15pt 0pt 18pt;line-height:normal;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">4.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 12pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Earnings Per Share</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We calculate basic income per share of common stock by dividing net income by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding for the period. We exclude non-vested shares of common stock issued in connection with our stock compensation plans from the calculation of the basic weighted-average common shares outstanding&nbsp;until those shares vest. 		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Amended Credit Facility</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">On September 30, 2013, the Company and its indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Guascor, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">amended and extended </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">its committed </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">credit agreement</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> (the &#x201C;Amended Credit Facility&#x201D;) with a syndicate of lenders</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, extending the final maturity date for the credit facility to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">September 30, 2018</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and increasing the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$700.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> U.S. dollar revolving credit facility by </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$400.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$1,100.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt -36pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Amended Credit Facility is comprised of revolving credit facilities, reflecting the newly increased $1,100.0 commitment and the existing </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x20AC;50.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> commitment, and a term loan facility comprised of tranche A and tranche B term loans denominated in U.S. dollars and euro</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, respectively. The term loans are subject to amortization in quarterly installments equal to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$2.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, with respect to the tranche A term loans, and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$3.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, with respect to the tranche B term loans. Any principal amount outstanding under the revolving credit facility and term loan facility is due and payable in full at maturit</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">y on September 30, 2018. At December 31</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, 2013, total outstanding borrowings under the Amended Credit Facility amounted to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$884</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">5</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, of which </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$588</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> was outstanding under the revolving credit facilities and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$295</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> was outstanding under the term loan facility. The Company had issued </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$85</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">5</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> in letters of credit under the revolving</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> credit facility at December 31</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, 2013. In addition to these letters of credit, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$221</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of letters of credit and bank guarantees</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> was outstanding at December 31</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, 2013, which were issued by banks offering uncommitted lines of credit.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Amended Credit Facility bear</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> interest, at the Company&#x2019;s election, at either (a) a rate equal to an applicable margin ranging from </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">1.75%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2.50%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, depending on the Company&#x2019;s leverage ratio, plus a LIBOR rate or (b) a rate equal to an applicable margin ranging from </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">0.75%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">1.50%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, depending on the Company&#x2019;s leverage ratio, plus a base rate as defined in the facility.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In addition to paying interest on outstanding principal under the Amended Credit Facility, the Company is required to pay a commitment fee under the revolving credit facility for unutilized commitments, and fees for outstanding performance and financial letters of credit.&nbsp;&nbsp;These fee amounts depend on the Company&#x2019;s leverage ratio and range from </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">0.375%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.50%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">per annum</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Amended Credit Facility requires that certain net proceeds related to asset sales, to the extent not reinvested in assets used or useful in the Company&#x2019;s business within one year, be used to pay down the outstanding balance. The Company may voluntarily prepay outstanding loans under the Amended Credit Facility at any time without premium or penalty, other than customary breakage costs. The Amended Credit Facility contains normal and customary covenants, including the provision of periodic financial information, financial covenants (including a maximum leverage ratio and a minimum interest coverage ratio), and certain other limitations governing, among others, such matters as the Company&#x2019;s ability to incur additional debt, grant liens on assets, make investments, acquisitions or mergers, dispose of assets, make capital expenditures, engage in transactions with affiliates, make amendments to documentation for the Company&#x2019;s 6 &#xBD;% Senior Subordinated Notes that would be materially adverse to lenders and pay dividends and distributions or repurchase capital stock. The Amended Credit Facility also provides for customary events of default. The Company was in compliance with the Amended Credit Facilit</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">y debt covenants at December 31</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, 2013.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In connection with executing the Amended Credit Facility, the Company incurred fees of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$5</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> which are being amortized utilizing the effective interest method over the term of the Amended Credit Facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fees totaling </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$3.4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> were amortized to earnings for fiscal year ended December 31, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Included in interest expense were commitment and letter of credit fees of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$4.7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$5.5</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> for the years ended December 31, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 2.15pt 0pt 18pt;line-height:normal;text-indent: -18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">12</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 12pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;"> Pension Plans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 2.15pt 0pt 0pt;line-height:normal;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Defined Benefit Plans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 2.15pt 0pt 0pt;line-height:normal;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company sponsors defined benefit pension plans at U.S. and non-U.S. locations. The U.S. qualified pension plan covers salaried, non-union hourly and certain bargaining unit employees. The benefits are largely frozen, with the exception of those for certain bargaining units, which accumulate according to a flat dollar formula that is not related to future earnings levels. Those employees whose benefits are frozen participate in a defined contribution plan. The defined benefit pension plans sponsored by the Company outside the U.S. are generally not frozen, with future benefits being determined using pensionable earnings and service at the time of determination.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company uses an annual measurement date of December&nbsp;31. The expected long-term rates of return on plan assets are determined as of the measurement date. The expected long-term rates of return are projected to be the rates of return to be earned over the period until the benefits are paid. Accordingly, the long-term rates of return should reflect the rates of return on present investments and expected contributions to be received during the current year and on reinvestments over the period. The rates of return utilized reflect the expected rates of return during the periods for which the payment of benefits is deferred. The expected long-term rate of return on plan assets used is based on what is realistically achievable based on the types of assets held by the plans and the plans&#x2019; investment policy. Historical asset return trends for the larger plans are reviewed over fifteen, ten and five years. The Company reviews each plan and its historical returns and asset allocations to determine the appropriate expected long-term rate of return on plan assets to be used. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The asset allocations of the Company&#x2019;s U.S. pension plans by asset category are as follows:</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">(1)</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 15pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">U.S. Fixed Income: Includes investments in the broad fixed income market such as government and agency bonds, mortgage bonds, and corporate bonds. Duration of the bonds may range from short (e.g., three months or less) to very long (e.g., 12 years or longer). Credit quality of U.S. Fixed Income is generally high quality in nature (e.g., AAA to BBB) but can also include lower quality or high yield bonds (e.g., BB or lower). Common indices are the Barclays Aggregate and Citigroup Broad Investment Grade Index. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 24.5pt;text-indent: -24.5pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">(2)</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 15pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Global Asset Allocations: Broadly diversified strategy where investment managers have the capacity to invest in multiple asset classes and the ability to alter asset class allocations with agreed tolerances. In some cases, there are no common indices for the assets in this asset class and typically a blended index of equities and fixed income is utilized, ex. 60% S&amp;P 500/40% Barclays Aggregate. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 2.15pt 0pt 0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Level 3 assets consist of annuities held as investments within the plan that cover a set amount of liabilities and the effect of changes in the values of the related assets and liabilities are generally offsetting.&nbsp;&nbsp;Level 3 assets also consist of annuities that require contribution premiums to fund ongoing liabilities as required by foreign governmental regulations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Annuities are valued using standard actuarial calculations such as discount rates, mortality rates and participant population.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 2.15pt 0pt 0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company&#x2019;s investment objectives in managing its defined benefit plan assets are to provide reasonable assurance that present and future benefit obligations to all participants and beneficiaries are met as they become due; to provide a total return that, over the long-term, maximizes the ratio of the plan assets to liabilities, while minimizing the present value of required Company contributions at the appropriate levels of risk; and to meet any statutory requirements, laws and local regulatory agencies&#x2019; requirements. Key investment decisions involving asset allocations, investment manager structure, investment managers, investment advisors and trustees or custodians are reviewed regularly. An asset liability modeling study is used as the basis for aggregated asset allocation decisions and updated approximately every five years or as required. The Company&#x2019;s current global asset allocation strategy for its pension plans is </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">60%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> in equity securities and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">40%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> in debt securities and cash excluding those assets in non-U.S. plans required by regulation to be in insurance contracts or other similar assets. The Company sets upper limits and lower limits of plus or minus 5%. The rebalancing strategy is reviewed quarterly if cash flows are not sufficient to rebalance the plans and appropriate action is taken to bring the plans within the strategic allocation ranges. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company&#x2019;s policy is to contribute to the U.S. qualified plan the amount necessary to maintain benefits under the Pension Protection Act of 2006, and additional discretionary amounts, up to the limitations imposed by the applicable tax codes. Contributions to the UK pension plans are determined in agreement with the plan trustees. Contributions to funded plans in other countries are based on applicable local funding requirements. The Company currently estimates that it will contribute to its U.S. and non-U.S. pension plans approximately</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$10.7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and $1.7, respectively, in 2014.</font>

		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The purpose of the Company&#x2019;s hedging activities is to mitigate the economic impact of changes in foreign currency exchange rates and interest rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company attempts to hedge transaction exposures through natural offsets.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the extent that this is not practicable, the Company may enter into forward exchange contracts or interest rate swaps.&nbsp;&nbsp;Major exposure areas considered for hedging include foreign currency denominated receivables and payables, firm committed transactions, forecast sales and purchases and variable interest rates.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">We are involved in various litigation, claims and administrative proceedings arising in the normal course of business. Amounts recorded for identified contingent liabilities are estimates, which are regularly reviewed and adjusted to reflect additional information when it becomes available. We are indemnified by our former owner, Ingersoll Rand Company Limited, for certain of these matters as part of Ingersoll Rand&#x2019;s sale of the Company and by the sellers of Grupo Guascor for certain of these matters in connection with our acquisition of Grupo Guascor, S.L. (&#x201C;Guascor&#x201D;) in May 2011.&nbsp;&nbsp;While adverse decisions in certain of these litigation matters, claims and administrative proceedings could have a material effect on a particular period&#x2019;s results of operations, subject to the uncertainties inherent in estimating future costs for contingent liabilities and the benefit of the indemnities</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">from Ingersoll Rand and the sellers of Guascor, management believes that any future accruals with respect to these currently known contingencies would not have a material effect on the financial condition, liquidity or cash flows of the Company.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:8.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">Painted Post Labor Litigation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:8.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In November 2007, Local 313 of IUE-CWA, the union that represents certain employees at the Company&#x2019;s Painted Post, New York, facility (the &#x201C;IUE&#x201D;) made an offer to have its striking members return to work under the terms of the previously expired union agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company rejected that offer and locked out these represented employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;Approximately one week later, after reaching an impasse in negotiations, the Company exercised its right to implement the terms of its last contract offer, ended the lockout, and the employees represented by the IUE agreed to return to work under the implemented terms.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subsequently, the IUE filed several unfair labor practice (&#x201C;ULP&#x201D;) charges against the Company with Region 3 of the National Labor Relations Board (&#x201C;NLRB&#x201D;), asserting multiple allegations arising from the protracted labor dispute, its termination, contract negotiations and related matters.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:8.25pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Region 3 of the NLRB decided to proceed to complaint on only one-third of the ULP allegations asserted by the IUE, while the remaining claims were dismissed.&nbsp;&nbsp;Notably, the NLRB found that many of the critical aspects of the Company&#x2019;s negotiations with the IUE were handled appropriately, including the NLRB&#x2019;s findings that the union&#x2019;s strike was not an unfair labor practice strike and the Company&#x2019;s declaration of impasse and its unilateral implementation of its last offer were lawful. The Company, therefore, continued to operate under a more contemporary and competitive implemented contract </font>
		</p>

process used to return employees to the facility after reaching impasse and lifting the lockout, and the termination of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">two</font><font with the law and that it will ultimately prevail with respect to these ULP allegations.&nbsp;&nbsp;The litigation process, including further appeals, could reasonably take </font><font style="display: time.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although the ultimate outcome of these matters cannot be ascertained at this time, it is the opinion of management that the resolution of such matters will not have a material adverse effect on the Company&#x2019;s financial condition.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">During July 2009, the Company received notification from the current plan trustees of one of its subsidiaries' pension plans in the UK that sex equalization under the plan may have been achieved later than originally expected.&nbsp;&nbsp;The third-party trustee at the time action was taken believes that it had taken the appropriate steps to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">amend properly</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> the plan as originally expected.&nbsp;&nbsp;In June 2012, interpretation proceedings commenced in the English High Court to determine whether sex equalization of the plan was correctly implemented.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company accrued </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">5.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">) to address its estimate of contingent exposure regarding this dispute over potential unequal treatment of men and women under the pension plan related to a period in the 1990s and is exploring its</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> rights against others.&nbsp;&nbsp;O</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">n</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> January 31, 2014, the High Court found that the sex equalization had been correctly implemented at the relevant time.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Accordingly</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, the Company does not believe that it has any further financial or legal exposure relating to this matter</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: 			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">Enviroil Italia, S.p.A. (&#x201C;Enviroil&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;"> Litigation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In March 1998, Enviroil, which became an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company in May 2011, in conjunction with the acquisition of Grupo Guascor, executed an agreement with the Italian Ministry of Economic Development (&#x201C;MISE&#x201D;) to construct a plant in Gela, Italy, for the production of heating gas oil from exhausted oil.&nbsp;&nbsp;In August 2007, following the completion of construction and upon commencement of the operation of the plant, an accident occurred and the plant&#x2019;s operations were discontinued. In November 2008, Enviroil proposed converting the plant into a facility for the manufacturing of solar panels, and this proposal was rejected by MISE.&nbsp;&nbsp;In January 2010, MISE issued a decree declaring Enviroil in default of the agreement and ordering Enviroil to reimburse MISE the approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x20AC;7.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> (approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">9.6</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">) paid to Enviroil under the agreement, as well as sanctions, interest and other related costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Enviroil initiated a proceeding in the Court of Caltanissetta requesting an order to suspend the effect of the MISE decree primarily based on Enviroil&#x2019;s proposed conversion of the plant.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Court of Caltanissetta rejected Enviroil&#x2019;s request by order issued in October 2010, and following an appeal by Enviroil, issued a second order in December 2010, denying the appeal.&nbsp;&nbsp;In June 2010, while the proceedings in the Court of Caltanissetta were still pending, Enviroil also initiated proceedings before the Lazio Administrative Court requesting the revocation of the MISE decree.&nbsp;&nbsp;In March 2011, Enviroil appealed the decree directly with MISE through an administrative procedure, and engaged in settlement negotiations with MISE. The Lazio Administrative Court held a hearing on this matter in October 2012 and issued a decision in November 2012 revoking the MISE decree issued in January 2010 and ordering MISE to reconsider the conversion proposal submitted by Enviroil in November 2008. Enviroil renewed settlement negotiations with MISE in October 2012, which concluded upon the parties reaching a settlement and entering into a settlement agreement in September 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Pursuant to this settlement agreement, </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">which has been approved by the Court of</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> Conti, MISE</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> agreed to waive sanctions, interest and other related costs, which the Company had previously accrued, in </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">exchange for which Enviroil paid to</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> MISE approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x20AC;7.3</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> (approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$10.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">) &nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 9.35pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">Banco Santos Litigation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 9.35pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In July 2004, Guascor SA and Jaguari Energetica SA, subsidiaries of Guascor (collectively, the &#x201C;GG Entities&#x201D;), entered into an agreement (the &#x201C;BNDES Agreement&#x201D;) with the Bank of National Economic and So</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">cial Development (&#x201C;BNDES&#x201D;) for </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">the construction of a power plant in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil (the &#x201C;Project&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Pursuant to the terms of the BNDES Agreement, in August 2004, the GG Entities entered into a separate agreement (the &#x201C;Banco Santos Agreement&#x201D;) with Banco Santos, a Brazilian bank previously based in Sao Paulo, Brazil.&nbsp;&nbsp;Per the terms of the Banco Santos Agreement, Banco Santos and the GG Entities agreed that: (i) in exchange for a fee paid by the GG Entities, Banco Santos would establish a reserve in favor of the GG Entities in the amount of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">R$3.6</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> (approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$1.5</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">) (the &#x201C;Reserve&#x201D;) to ensure that funds for a </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">twelve</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> month term would be available</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> (if needed) by the GG Entities</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> to fund their performance obligations under the BNDES Agreement; (ii) the GG Entities would issue </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">twelve</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> banking credit notes (the &#x201C;Notes&#x201D;) to Banco Santos (</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">one</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> for each of the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">twelve</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> months), under which Notes the GG Entities would be obligated to make a payment to Banco Santos if the GG Entities used the applicable portion of the Reserve associated with a Note; and (iii) no portion of the Reserve would be invested by Banco Santos in any high risk investments.&nbsp;&nbsp;The GG Entities completed the Project in December 2006 and fulfilled their obligations under the BNDES Agreement, without using any portion of the Reserve.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accordingly, we believe that, pursuant to the terms of the Banco Santos Agreement, none of the Notes securing the Reserve became due or payable by the GG Entities to Banco Santos.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In September 2004, Banco Santos, without the knowledge or consent of the GG Entities, transferred the Reserve to its affiliates, Santos Credit Yield (&#x201C;SCY&#x201D;) and Santos Credit Master (&#x201C;SCM,&#x201D; and together with SCY, the &#x201C;BS Affiliates&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon the receipt of the Reserve, the BS Affiliates invested the funds in a high risk investment, resulting in the loss of the entire Reserve.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, concurrently with the transfer of the Reserve, Banco Santos assigned its rights in the Notes to the BS Affiliates.&nbsp;&nbsp;Shortly after the assignment of the Notes, Banco Santos declared bankruptcy.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The GG Entities commenced an action (the &#x201C;Declaratory Action&#x201D;) in the Civil Courts in the State of Sao Paulo, Brazil, in April 2005 seeking a declaratory judgment that the BS Affiliates were barred from recovering any amounts with regard to the Notes because such Notes were null and void pursuant to the terms of the Banco Santos Agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the fourth quarter of 2012, the Court appointed an expert to evaluate the GG Entities&#x2019; claims and allegations. However, notwithstanding the issuance of an expert&#x2019;s report that was favorable to the GG Entities, the Court denied the declaratory relief sought by the GG Entities and ordered the GG Entities to pay attorneys&#x2019; fees.&nbsp;&nbsp;The GG Entities timely appealed the adverse judgment in August 2013, which appeal is currently pending.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">In December 2010, while the Declaratory Action was still pending, the BS Affiliates filed a separate action (the &#x201C;BS Action&#x201D;) in the Sao Paulo Civil Court seeking to recover from the GG Entities the amount of the Reserve.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Court stayed the BS Action in September 2011 pending a final ruling in the Declaratory Action.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Although we believe, based on the factual circumstances and the applicable law, that Banco Santos and the BS Affiliates violated the terms of the Banco Santos Agreement and the payment terms of the Notes, and that the GG Entities should prevail in both Declaratory Action and the BS Action, the ultimate outcome of these proceedings cannot be ascertained at this time.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company estimates that the total aggregate exposure for damages, interest and attorneys&#x2019; fees could be up to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">R$37.5</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> (approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$15.9)</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Moreover, the Company has an indemnification claim against the sellers of Guascor with regard to this matter.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;text-decoration:underline;">Italian Value-Added Tax Claim</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company is in litigation with the Italian tax authorities regarding value-added taxes for tax years 2005-2008 and the application of Italian and European Union laws.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company received an adverse judgment in February 2012 for tax years 2005-2006 for approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x20AC;4.2</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> ($</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">5.8</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">).&nbsp;&nbsp;In July 2012, the Company appealed the judgment and continues to believe that it will prevail on its position that no tax is owed.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company estimates the total aggregate exposure for taxes, interest and penalties could be up to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x20AC;10.1</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> ($</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">13.9</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">).</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:4.5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">On December&nbsp;28, 2007, the Company executed a lease transaction including a committed line of credit of up to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x20AC;23.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> (approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$31.6)</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> that was used to fund construction of a new compressor testing facility (the &#x201C;Facility&#x201D;) in close proximity to the Company&#x2019;s operation in France. The Company began leasing the Facility in January 2010, and is required to pay rent during the initial base term of the lease in an amount equal to the aggregate amount of interest payable by the lessor on the outstanding principal amount of the debt incurred by the lessor. Interest is determined by reference to the EURIBOR Rate plus an applicable margin of between </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">1.25%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">2.50%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">. The initial base term of the lease expires in February 2015. At maturity, the Company may either terminate or, subject to the mutual agreement, extend the lease. The Company may purchase the Facility at any time for the amount of the lessor&#x2019;s debt outstanding, including upon maturity of the lease. If the lease is terminated, the Company has guaranteed that the lessor will receive at least </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">80%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> of the cost of the Facility upon the sale of the Facility. The Company anticipates that the lease will mature in 2015. The operating lease contains representations, warranties and covenants typical of such leases. Any event of default could accelerate the Company&#x2019;s payments under the terms of the lease. </font>

Total rental expense relating to th</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ese leases was approximately </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$28.9</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$25.4</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$27.7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, 2012 and 2011, respectively. 			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The options and stock appreciation rights granted have a </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">10</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;year contract term. Restricted stock, options and stock appreciation rights granted prior to 2010 vest over a </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">four</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> year period. Beginning in 2010, the Company granted restricted stock, options and stock appreciation rights which vest over a </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">three</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> year period, as well as Performance Restricted Stock Units (&#x201C;PRSUs&#x201D;). PRSUs vest annually over a </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">three</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> year period to the extent that the percentile rank of the shareholder return of the Company&#x2019;s stock is at or above the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">25th</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> percentile of a selected peer group, with </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">16.67%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> vesting if such percentile rank is at this threshold level and up to </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">50.00%</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> vesting if such percentile rank is at or above the </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">75th</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> percentile of the selected peer group.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 2.15pt 0pt 0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 2.15pt 0pt 0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">These functions have been defined as the operating segments of the Company because they are the segments (1) that engage in business activities from which revenues are earned and expenses are incurred; (2) whose operating results are regularly reviewed by the Corporation&#x2019;s chief operating decision maker to make decisions about resources to be allocated to the segment and assess its performance; and (3) for which discrete financial information is available.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">Unallocated amounts represent expenses and assets that cannot be assigned directly to either reportable segment because of their nature.&nbsp;&nbsp;Unallocated net expenses include certain corporate expenses and research and development expenses.&nbsp;&nbsp;Assets that are directly assigned to the two reportable segments are trade accounts receivable, net inventories and goodwill.&nbsp;&nbsp;Unallocated assets include cash, prepaid expenses and other, deferred taxes, property, plant and equipment and intangible assets. There are no significant intercompany transactions between our reportable segments.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">25.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subsequent Event</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company owns and operates six pig manure treatment facilities in Spain which it acquired in its acquisition of Guascor. The Spanish government published a draft regulation at the end of January 2014 that reflects a reduction in the tariffs of approximately 37%, which, if enacted, would be retroactive to J</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">uly 2013. In view of the proposed</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> change in the tariffs, the Company has decided to suspend the operations at its six facilities, although discussions with the Spanish government are ongoing. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The draft regulation is a clarification of a law that was passed in 2013 as the law did not have sufficient specificity to reasonably estimate the tariff.&nbsp;&nbsp;Consequently, the Company believes an impairment triggering event occurred in 2013 and has recor</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">ded an impairment charge of </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$40</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> in 2013 to reduce the value of the property, plant and equipment. At the time of the acquisition, the Company did not record any specific intangible assets related to the pig manure treatment facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Also in connection with the draft regulation being issued, the Company has reduced its 2013 revenues and gross margin by approximately $23.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">7</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$22</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">0</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">, respectively, for the retroactive reduction of the tariffs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 12pt">
			&nbsp;
		</p></div><div style="margin-left:57pt;margin-right:57pt;">
